title: Supervising Compliance in Practice: Masterclass Series
summary: Ten half-day masterclasses showing supervisors how to test whether firms' compliance arrangements work in practice across core compliance areas.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors to assess whether firms' compliance arrangements work in practice, not just on paper, across ten core areas from the compliance function and AML/CFT to complaints, outsourcing, reporting and compliance culture.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a practical understanding of how firms build and run their compliance arrangements, and how to test them on the supervisor's side of the table. Participants leave able to judge whether arrangements are effective, spot the red flags of paper compliance and frame proportionate supervisory responses.
sections.What It Covers: The compliance function and monitoring programmes, AML/CFT compliance, conduct of business and suitability, complaints handling, outsourcing, governance and fitness and propriety, regulatory reporting, conflicts of interest, data protection and record-keeping, and compliance culture.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for assessing firms' compliance and control arrangements
AML/CFT, conduct and governance specialists who review firms' policies, procedures and testing
Newer supervisors and staff moving into supervision from compliance roles in industry
Learning Objectives: Explain what effective compliance arrangements look like across the main areas of firm activity
Assess the independence, resourcing and effectiveness of the compliance function
Evaluate firms' policies, monitoring and testing against how they operate in practice
Identify red flags of paper compliance, weak controls and poor customer outcomes
Challenge senior management and control functions using targeted supervisory questions
Formulate proportionate findings and supervisory responses for compliance weaknesses
sections.Structure and Format: Ten half-day masterclasses of about three and a half hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, as a complete series or as standalone sessions. Each masterclass combines a short briefing with case studies, sample file exercises and a supervisory question set, and masterclasses can be selected or tailored to the authority's priorities.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervision or of compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. Each masterclass is self-contained, so no prior attendance is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Compliance and the Compliance Function in Banks (2005)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)

modules.title: The Compliance Function and Monitoring Programmes
modules.summary: How to assess the mandate, independence, resourcing and reporting lines of a firm's compliance function, and whether its risk-based monitoring programme provides real assurance.
objectives: Assess the independence, authority and resourcing of the compliance function
Evaluate the design and coverage of a compliance monitoring programme
Judge whether compliance reporting gives the board an accurate picture
syllabus: Compliance mandate, reporting lines and the head of compliance role
Compliance risk assessment and the risk-based monitoring plan
Testing methodology, findings tracking and reporting to the board
Red flags: under-resourcing, outsourced compliance and box-ticking

modules.title: Supervising AML/CFT Compliance Arrangements
modules.summary: How to assess a firm's business-wide risk assessment, customer due diligence, monitoring and reporting arrangements against the FATF Recommendations and the risk-based approach.
objectives: Evaluate a firm's business-wide and customer risk assessments
Assess customer due diligence, transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting
Identify the red flags of an ineffective AML/CFT framework
syllabus: The risk-based approach and the business-wide risk assessment
Customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring
Suspicious activity reporting to the national FIU and the MLRO role
Sample testing of customer files and alert handling

modules.title: Conduct of Business and Suitability
modules.summary: How to supervise firms' conduct of business arrangements, including client categorisation, disclosure, suitability and appropriateness assessments, and fair treatment of customers.
objectives: Explain the core conduct of business obligations owed to clients
Assess suitability and appropriateness processes and file quality
Identify conduct risks arising from advice and distribution models
syllabus: Client categorisation, disclosure and fair, clear and not misleading communications
Suitability and appropriateness: process, evidence and file reviews
Advice and distribution models and their conduct risks
Sample testing of client files: what good and poor look like

modules.title: Complaints Handling and Root-Cause Analysis
modules.summary: How to assess whether a firm handles complaints fairly and promptly, analyses root causes, and uses complaints data to improve products, services and customer outcomes.
objectives: Evaluate the fairness and timeliness of a firm's complaints process
Assess the quality of root-cause analysis and management information
Use complaints data as an indicator of wider conduct risk
syllabus: Complaints policies, timelines, redress and escalation to dispute resolution schemes
Complaints classification, recording and management information
Root-cause analysis and feedback into products and processes
Complaints as a proxy for culture and conduct risk

modules.title: Outsourcing and Third-Party Arrangements
modules.summary: How to supervise firms' outsourcing and third-party arrangements, from due diligence and contracts to oversight, concentration risk and exit planning, where responsibility stays with the firm.
objectives: Explain why regulatory responsibility cannot be outsourced
Assess due diligence, contractual safeguards and ongoing oversight
Evaluate concentration risk, sub-outsourcing and exit strategies
syllabus: Material and critical outsourcing: identification and notification
Due diligence, contracts, audit and access rights
Ongoing oversight, performance monitoring and intra-group arrangements
Concentration, sub-outsourcing and exit planning

modules.title: Governance and Fitness and Propriety
modules.summary: How to assess board composition, challenge and accountability, and whether the firm's arrangements for assessing the fitness and propriety of key individuals are robust and ongoing.
objectives: Assess board composition, committee structure and quality of challenge
Evaluate the firm's own fitness and propriety assessments of key individuals
Identify governance weaknesses that undermine compliance
syllabus: Board structure, independence, committees and senior manager accountability
Board papers, minutes and evidence of effective challenge
Fitness and propriety: competence, integrity, financial soundness and time commitment
Red flags: dominant individuals, weak challenge and rubber-stamping

modules.title: Regulatory Reporting and Data Quality
modules.summary: How to assess the governance, controls and data lineage behind firms' regulatory returns, and why late, inaccurate or inconsistent reporting signals deeper control weaknesses.
objectives: Explain the supervisory reliance placed on regulatory returns
Assess governance, reconciliation and sign-off controls over reporting
Identify data quality red flags and frame a supervisory response
syllabus: Regulatory returns and their role in risk-based supervision
Reporting governance: ownership, review and sign-off
Data lineage, reconciliations and end-user computing risk
Resubmissions, errors and breaches: supervisory follow-up

modules.title: Conflicts of Interest
modules.summary: How to assess whether firms identify, prevent and manage conflicts of interest across their business, including inducements, personal account dealing and group relationships.
objectives: Identify the main sources of conflicts of interest in regulated firms
Evaluate conflicts policies, registers and management arrangements
Assess when disclosure is an inadequate response to a conflict
syllabus: Sources of conflict: remuneration, inducements, group and personal interests
Conflicts policies, registers and information barriers
Personal account dealing, gifts and hospitality
Disclosure as a last resort: when it is not enough

modules.title: Data Protection and Record-Keeping
modules.summary: How to assess firms' record-keeping arrangements and their handling of customer data, so that records are complete, retrievable and protected, and evidence the firm's compliance.
objectives: Explain record-keeping obligations and their importance to supervision
Assess data protection governance and the handling of customer data
Evaluate whether records are complete, retrievable and secure
syllabus: Record-keeping requirements: transactions, communications and decisions
Data protection principles and governance in regulated firms
Data breaches, incident response and notification
Testing record retrieval during inspections

modules.title: Compliance Culture: Masterclass and Capstone
modules.summary: Brings the series together by examining how compliance culture shows itself in behaviour, incentives and tone from the top, and applies the full series to an integrated firm case study.
objectives: Assess indicators of a firm's compliance culture
Integrate findings across compliance areas into an overall view
Formulate proportionate supervisory responses and follow-up
syllabus: Tone from the top and the middle: culture in practice
Incentives, speaking up and breach reporting as cultural indicators
From individual weaknesses to an overall compliance risk assessment
Workshop: integrated firm case study and supervisory action plan

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.

related.title: Core Supervisory Skills: Business Models, Governance and Risk Governance Panels
related.summary: A three-day workshop taking supervisors from business model analysis through governance interviews to a risk governance panel, using running case studies and role plays.

related.title: How Financial Firms Work: Business Models and Financial Statements for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping supervisors understand how financial firms make money, read their accounts and identify capital, liquidity and business model risks.

related.title: Supervisory Risk Assessment Toolkit
related.summary: A ten-module toolkit taking supervisors through the full firm risk assessment cycle, from business model and governance analysis to panels, risk ratings and findings.

related.title: Foundations of Financial Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An eight-module induction for new regulatory staff covering why we regulate, the authority's powers, risk-based supervision and a first supervisory case.

related.title: Core Professional Skills for Regulatory Staff
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme building the core writing, analysis, meeting, challenge, presentation and data skills that regulatory staff need every day.
